newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea and cabinet ministers Ulm Spineanu, Mircea Ciumara and Calin Popescu Tariceanu are meeting the leaders of Romania's largest trade unions federations following Monday's talks with representatives of the International Monetary Fund.
They are expected to debate salary indexations.
* Union leaders have warned that real reform and restructuring have failed to affect the industrial sector.
* Road transport trade unions strongly oppose a road tax expected to become effective on August 1, fearing that money raised would be used for purposes other than road repairs.

* The Cement trade unions federation -- based in the eastern town of Medgidia -- has announced that employees of the Romcim SA cement maker will launch protests, including marches in central Bucharest and strikes, to demand proper social protection measures ahead of plans to privatise the company.
They want their jobs to be secure for at least three years after Romcim shifts to private hands and demand that the new owner be obliged to remain in the sector.
Unionists also want employees to be allowed to buy shares.
* Romania's June industrial output rose by 2.6 percent against May but posted a 3.8 percent drop year-on-year, the National Statistics Commission said.
Output in most industrial sectors fell, especially the energy sector.
* Average wage rose by 2.3 percent in June from May.
* Eight coal miners from the Vulcan mine in the Jiu Valley were taken to hospital after an explosion caused by a gas leak.
Four are in critical conditions with burns over almost their entire body. The other four sustained less serious injuries but suffered from carbon monoxide poisoning.
